d: PIPECARE Group is looking for an experienced Global Logistics Manager to join our team in UAE.

By providing technology and service focused solutions to the international arena of the oil and gas industry, the PIPECARE Group of companies has been helping our customers ensure the integrity of their pipeline and facility assets for over 25 years.
Industry / sector: Oil & Gas / In Line Inspection services.

PIPECARE Group provides in-line pipeline inspection and integrity services to pipeline operators worldwide. Our business depends on moving high value inspection tools and technical equipment across borders, to a schedule, and bringing them back again. Every inspection campaign begins and ends with a logistics movement, and a tool held in customs is a project that does not start.

The Group operates through five regional business units covering Europe and Africa, the Gulf, India and the Far East, the Western Hemisphere, and our technology centre. Tools move continuously between these regions, which makes temporary admission, customs compliance and transit planning central to how the business performs rather than a back office function.
We are strengthening the central supply chain function and are looking for a logistics specialist of real depth to take ownership of international movement across the Group.

The Global Logistics Manager is responsible for all international movement of inspection tools, spares, consumables and technical equipment across the Group, together with the customs, documentation and compliance that surround it.
q: At least eight years in international logistics, with substantial experience moving high value technical or industrial equipment rather than general cargo or consumer freight.

Demonstrable hands on ownership of temporary import and export regimes, including ATA Carnets, temporary admission and re-export. This is the single most important requirement and candidates should be able to describe specific movements they have run.
Strong customs knowledge with a working understanding of how clearance actually happens in difficult jurisdictions.
Dangerous goods certification, IATA DGR or IMDG, with practical experience shipping lithium batteries.
Proven record negotiating with and managing freight forwarders and customs brokers, including rate negotiation and service level enforcement.
Comfortable owning a problem end to end, working to operational deadlines, and being measured on cost and on time delivery.
Background in oilfield services, non destructive testing, inspection, survey or another business that operates a mobile fleet of high value equipment.
Experience with free zone regimes, for example Jebel Ali, DMCC or Aqaba, and with hub and consolidation strategies.
Exposure to sanctions and export control screening.
Experience implementing or operating logistics modules within an ERP.
A professional qualification such as CIPS, APICS CLTD or FIATA.
Lifting and Carrying: Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds
Mobility: Must be able to walk and climb to perform duties, including maneuvering within a refinery or plant environment and accessing elevated platforms via ladders and stairwells
Communication: Sufficient clarity of speech and hearing, or other communication capabilities, to communicate effectively
Focus and Multitasking: Ability to maintain focus and multitask effectively
Safety Equipment: Must be able to wear safety equipment as required by the safety department for personal protection, if/where needed in manufacturing environments.
Personal Mobility and Reflexes: Sufficient personal mobility and physical reflexes, with or without reasonable accommodations, to perform office duties and travel to off-site locations when necessary

r: International movement of the tool fleet
Plan and execute the movement of inspection tools between regions, bases and job sites, to the dates committed in the operational schedule.
Work with tool management and the regional units to sequence movements so that tool availability supports the campaign plan rather than constraining it.
Own the end to end transit plan for each movement, including routing, mode selection, consolidation, lead times and contingency.
Reduce the time tools spend in transit and in customs, both of which are lost utilization.

Own temporary import and export across all operating jurisdictions, including ATA Carnets, temporary admission bonds, re-export guarantees and duty relief, so that equipment entering a country for a campaign leaves it again without unnecessary cost or delay.
Build and maintain a country pair customs and transit reference covering documentation, duties, lead times, restrictions and local agent requirements.
Manage dangerous goods movements, in particular lithium batteries and any regulated materials carried within inspection tools, in full compliance with IATA and IMDG requirements.
Carry out sanctions, export control and dual use screening on movements and counterparties, and escalate anything requiring a Group decision.
Resolve detentions, demurrage, inspections and customs queries quickly, and identify the root cause so that the same problem does not recur.
Select, negotiate with and manage freight forwarders, customs brokers, handling agents and couriers, and hold them to agreed service levels.
Deliver measurable reduction in landed logistics cost per movement against budgets set by Finance, without compromising schedule or compliance.
Validate freight invoices, challenge incorrect charges and ensure accruals and cost allocation reflect what actually moved and for which project.
Bring logistics into the Group ERP, including tool allocation, shipment tracking, freight cost capture and temporary import status, and ensure the data stays accurate once it is there.
Maintain a single reliable view of where every tool is, what status it holds in customs, and when it becomes available again.
Write and embed the standard operating procedures for shipping, documentation, packing and receipt across all locations.
Ensure cargo insurance is adequate and correctly declared, and manage claims where loss or damage occurs.
Identify concentration risks in routes, agents and jurisdictions, and build practical alternatives before they are needed.
This role sits within the central supply chain function and operates under the Group's separation of duties. The boundaries below are deliberate.
The role holds no spend approval authority. Budgets for logistics and freight are set and approved by Finance. The role delivers optimization and savings against those budgets.
Logistics costs are independently verified by the cost controllers at the Commercial Control Centre. The role owns the movement of goods, Finance owns what it is permitted to cost.
The role does not own procurement of parts, tools or services, which sits elsewhere in the function, although close coordination is expected.
